title: First Bad Version

content.problemStatement:
You have `n` versions of a product, numbered 1 to n, released in order.
At some point a bug was introduced, so every version from a certain
version onward is bad, and every version before it is good. You're given
`n` and the first bad version directly as `bad`, standing in for a
version check you'd normally call one version at a time.

**Find and return the first bad version, using as few version checks as possible.**
constraints: every version >= bad is bad, every version < bad is good
content.inputFormat: Single line: JSON array of all arguments, e.g. [arg1, arg2, ...]

sampleTestCases.explanation: versions 1-3 are good, versions 4-5 are bad, so the first bad one is 4
the only version is already bad
only the very last version is bad

code.Python3:
# Time:  O(logn)
# Space: O(1)

class Solution(object):
    def firstBadVersion(self, n):
        """
        :type n: int
        :rtype: int
        """
        left, right = 1, n
        while left <= right:
            mid = left + (right - left) / 2
            if isBadVersion(mid): # noqa
                right = mid - 1
            else:
                left = mid + 1
        return left

hints: Identify the search space and verify that the condition is monotonic (true...true...false...false).
Be mindful of integer overflow when computing mid: use mid = left + (right - left) // 2.
Ensure the termination condition (left <= right vs left < right) correctly handles boundary elements.
